title: Effect of Sintering Temperature on the Microstructure and Integrated Properties of MgAlTiVFeCo Lightweight High-Entropy Alloy

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Equiatomic (or near‑equiatomic) elemental powders of Mg, Al, Ti, V, Fe, and Co with high purity, blended and often mechanically alloyed (ball‑milled) prior to consolidation to form a lightweight high‑entropy alloy feedstock.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Powder metallurgy consolidation by spark plasma sintering (SPS) under vacuum/inert atmosphere with uniaxial pressure (≈30–50 MPa), varying the sintering temperature (≈600–1000 °C) and short holds (≈5–10 min) to study densification and phase evolution; possible post‑sinter anneal/temper for stress relief.
recollection.structure: Guess: Temperature‑dependent multiphase microstructure: at lower T, a fine BCC‑dominant solid solution with residual porosity; at intermediate T, a dual‑phase BCC matrix with dispersed Laves (C14/C15) intermetallics and refined grains; at higher T, increased Laves fraction and coarsening, occasional segregation and reduced Mg content, plus trace oxide dispersoids (e.g., MgO/Al2O3) from residual oxygen. Overall density increases with T, but excessive T yields coarser, more brittle structures.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Sintering temperature governs densification and phase stability via a combination of (i) transient liquid‑phase sintering near the Mg/Al melting range that accelerates neck growth and pore elimination, (ii) diffusion‑driven solid‑solution formation and subsequent precipitation of Laves phases from the BCC matrix, (iii) Hall–Petch strengthening from grain refinement at optimal T, (iv) solid‑solution strengthening from Ti/V/Fe/Co in the BCC lattice, (v) dispersion strengthening from fine oxides, and (vi) Mg volatilization at higher T that shifts composition, promotes Laves enrichment, and embrittles the alloy. The balance between densification and coarsening sets the property maxima at intermediate temperatures.
recollection.results: Guess: Relative density rises from roughly 90–92% at ≈650–700 °C to ≈98–99% at ≈850–900 °C; hardness increases with temperature to a peak then drops with coarsening (peak Vickers hardness on the order of 500–650 HV at intermediate T); room‑temperature compressive yield strength peaks around 1.1–1.5 GPa with plastic strain ~10–20% at the optimal sintering window; density remains in the lightweight range (~4.8–5.5 g/cm³). Specific strength is maximized near the intermediate T due to a fine BCC + Laves microstructure. At the highest T, Mg loss and Laves coarsening reduce ductility and may slightly lower hardness/strength despite higher densification; wear and corrosion resistances track densification and phase balance, with best integrated properties near ~800–900 °C.

score.note: Correctly identifies SPS with temperature variation up to 1000 °C. The structure description only generically captures increasing densification and possible oxide dispersoids; its BCC/Laves-phase and intermediate-temperature optimum narrative does not match the dense 1000 °C microstructure with uniformly distributed AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3 barrier phases. It misses the passive-film/Cl− blocking corrosion mechanism and parabolic, diffusion-controlled oxidation. Numerical predictions are substantially wrong: the actual optimum was 96.7% density and 1235.5 HV at 1000 °C, and the oxidation and corrosion values are omitted.
